draft.title: How governments intervene
card: Budget
The government raises money through taxes and spends it on things such as health, schools and roads. Changing taxes and spending changes how much money moves through the economy.
Laws and regulation
Governments make rules that businesses and people must follow, such as consumer protection laws and limits on pollution. Rules set the standards for how the market works.
Payments
The government pays money to people, such as the Age Pension and JobSeeker. These payments support people's incomes and are paid for from tax.
Interest rates
The Reserve Bank of Australia is not part of the budget. It sets the cash rate, which influences the interest rates banks charge on loans.
draft.remember: Governments act through the budget, laws, payments and, with the Reserve Bank, interest rates.

a.q: Which action is the Reserve Bank of Australia responsible for?
opts: Setting the cash rate that influences loan interest rates
Setting the rate of income tax paid by workers
Deciding how much is spent on public hospitals
Passing laws that protect consumers from false claims
a.why: The Reserve Bank sets the cash rate, which influences the interest rates banks charge on loans. Income tax and spending are decided through the budget, and consumer laws are made by governments.
a.clue: Think about who is not part of the budget.

b.q: A state government makes a rule that a factory must limit the pollution it puts into a river. Which way of intervening is this?
opts: Laws and regulation
Spending in the budget
Welfare payments
Setting interest rates
b.why: A rule that businesses must follow is a law or regulation. It is not spending or a payment, because the government is not handing over money, and it is not an interest rate decision.
b.clue: The factory must follow a rule.

a.best: Setting the cash rate that influences loan interest rates

problems.detail: "Governments act ... with the Reserve Bank, interest rates" suggests governments set interest rates jointly with the RBA. The card and the chapter point say the Reserve Bank sets the cash rate itself, separate from the budget. The RBA is independent of the government.

The stem says the government "makes a rule" and the clue repeats "must follow a rule". Both echo the card's wording for laws and regulation ("rules that businesses and people must follow"), so students can match words instead of understanding the idea.

b.q: A state government stops cafés from handing out single-use plastic straws to customers. Which way of intervening is this?

Welfare payments
Setting interest rates
